output.text: The morning fog had not yet lifted when the group gathered near the old oak by the trailhead. Assume that Alma is the head judge. Vik had arrived early, carrying a canvas bag slung over one shoulder, and he chatted quietly with Nell about the migratory patterns of warblers. Vik brought the first-aid kit. Leo, who had joined the walk for the first time, seemed a little unsure of the route markers, so Alma pointed out the trail signs to help him along. The group paused at a clearing where a heron stood motionless in the shallow water, and everyone lifted their binoculars at once. Hana finished ahead of Nell. Nell mentioned that she had seen a similar heron the previous spring, near a different pond entirely. As the path narrowed through the birch trees, Vik pointed out a woodpecker tapping steadily against a dead trunk, and Alma noted its rhythm in a small notebook. Nell finished ahead of Leo. Hana walked with a steady pace, pausing now and then to sketch a quick outline of a sparrow perched on a fence post. Leo carried a thermos of tea that he shared with the others once they reached the overlook, where the valley spread out in soft shades of green and gold. Hana finished ahead of Leo. By midday, the group had counted over twenty species, and Alma read the tally aloud while the others rested on a fallen log. Vik suggested they return the following weekend, and everyone agreed it had been a fine morning for birds.
